jobs.prompt:
refactor(cpp): replace five small hand-written runtime helpers with standard library facilities

CONTINUATION NOTICE: one or more earlier agents worked on this same task and were cut off by a dropped model connection. The branch you start from already contains everything they committed (their report file under cpp/gateway/docs/findings/ says how far they got; keep that file name and append to it). Do not start over: read the report and `git log` first, verify the tree builds, then continue from where they stopped. Commit small steps often.

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
Branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` contains `cpp/gateway/`: a finished module-for-module C++20 port of this repository's first-party TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`, `lib/jev_compaction/`): 325 application modules (`cpp/gateway/include/uos/**`, `cpp/gateway/src/**`), a JavaScript-semantics runtime layer `uos::rt` (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`) and 441 test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`, each a standalone program using the tiny harness `include/uos/rt/test.hpp`). The TypeScript is the behavioural ORACLE: expected values in tests were recorded from Bun 1.4.0, and the port reproduces Bun's observable behaviour. The optimised release build passes all 441 binaries / 5,023 cases on Linux ARM64 (GCC 16) and on macOS ARM64. Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM.

THE PROGRAMME YOU ARE PART OF
The owner's policy: generic functionality must come from mature open-source libraries, not hand-written code. `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md` ranks 55 runtime components with a verdict each; READ IT FIRST, then the row(s) for your component. JSON parsing (simdjson) and base64 (simdutf) are already done and are your worked examples: see `src/rt/json.cpp`, `src/rt/json_simdjson.hpp`, `src/rt/base64.cpp`, `third_party/simdjson`, `third_party/simdutf`, and how `CMakeLists.txt` registers third-party static libraries. About ten other agents are replacing OTHER components at the same time, each on its own clone; your branch will be merged with theirs, so stay strictly inside your OWNED paths and line ranges and keep unrelated code byte-identical (no reformatting, no renames, no drive-by fixes).

ALSO READ: `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (coroutine rules are mandatory: never bind structured bindings directly to a `co_await` result, never capture into a coroutine lambda that can outlive its frame), `cpp/gateway/docs/PORT-NOTES.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/TESTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md`. PORTING.md's "Host safety" rules and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" apply to the authors' production server, NOT to your disposable runner: use compilers directly, in parallel. `tools/unit.sh`, `tools/env.sh` and the CMake presets contain host-specific absolute paths; do not depend on them. `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` plus the vendored libraries that first-party code includes link into every test. `cpp/gateway/tools/ci_sanitize.py` is a small portable builder/runner (ASan+UBSan) you can copy the approach from: it resolves sources, compiles each once, links one binary per test.

YOUR MACHINE: a fresh GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its distribution packages are too old for this tree (it needs Boost >= 1.86 with Boost.JSON, and a C++20 compiler newer than GCC 12 / Clang 18): install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), and build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive under a temp directory. Also needed: OpenSSL 3, SQLite >= 3.40, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages. Port flags: `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion -Werror -DBOOST_JSON_NO_LIB -DBOOST_CONTAINER_NO_LIB -DBOOST_SYSTEM_NO_LIB -DBOOST_ASIO_DISABLE_AWAITABLE_FRAME_RECYCLING -DUOS_GATEWAY_NATIVE_LIBRARIES=1 -I cpp/gateway/include -I cpp/gateway`; third-party sources are compiled without the warning flags. Bun 1.4.0 is the oracle runtime: install exactly that version and, whenever you need to know what JavaScript does, RUN the TypeScript or a snippet under `bun --no-env-file`, do not guess.

RULES (owner policy as of 2026-11-17 22:30 UTC: "I don't care about parity, just make the system work with standard open-source modules")
- The LIBRARY'S standard behaviour is now the reference for generic functionality. Exact parity with Bun's quirks is NO LONGER REQUIRED. Make the library the implementation, delete the hand-written code, and do not build shims to reproduce Bun-specific edge cases, error-message wording, or leniencies.
- What must still hold, because "the system must work": (a) the gateway's own behaviour: every application-level test (anything outside `cpp/gateway/tests/rt/` and the test files named after your component) must still pass, since those encode what clients, providers and stored data need; if one fails after your swap, look at WHY: if it depends on a real functional property (a wire format, a status code, a header a client needs, a stored-data format, an authentication or validation decision), keep that property with the smallest adapter; if it only asserts a Bun-specific message string or an edge case no real client depends on, update the expectation; (b) SECURITY never gets weaker: where the library is more permissive than the current code on untrusted input, add the explicit check or pick the library's strict mode; being stricter than before is fine; (c) the public C++ API your component exposes to the rest of the port stays source-compatible unless changing it is clearly simpler, in which case update all callers (they are in your scope for that purpose only).
- Tests of your component itself (`tests/rt/<component>*_test.cpp`, its differential vectors): keep every case whose expectation the library also satisfies; for cases where the standard library behaviour differs from the Bun-recorded value, change the expectation to the library's result and record EACH class of change in `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` (create it if missing; append a section for your component: what differs, one example, why it is acceptable). Do not delete tests to make them pass; do not change expectations in bulk without classifying them.
- Vendor each library UNMODIFIED under `cpp/gateway/third_party/<name>/` with its LICENSE, a `PROVENANCE.md` (upstream URL, tag, date, how obtained) and `SHA256SUMS`; download the exact release named in your task and verify the SHA-256 given there. Register it the way simdjson and simdutf are registered: `cpp/gateway/CMakeLists.txt`, `cpp/gateway/tools/vendor_sources.py` and `cpp/gateway/cmake/vendors.json` (you may edit those three for registration only). Libraries already in the build (Boost 1.92, OpenSSL, ICU, zlib) are used as they are.
- ACCEPTANCE: (1) builds with the port flags without warnings (third-party code is exempt from the warning set); (2) your component's tests pass with expectations updated per the rule above, and every other test whose link list includes your files passes, plain and under `-fsanitize=address,undefined`; build and run as much of the whole suite as your time allows and report exact counts; (3) add a robustness harness `cpp/gateway/fuzz/<component>_library.cpp` in the style of the existing files in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/` that feeds arbitrary bytes through the new implementation's public entry points (it must only return or throw the port's ordinary JavaScript-style errors), register it in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/targets.json` with an `extra_sources` list and add a few seed inputs under `cpp/gateway/fuzz/corpus/<target>/`; build it and run it for two minutes as a smoke check, the maintainer's CI runs it longer; (4) measure old vs new on representative inputs (ns/op, allocations) and put the table in your report; (5) DELETE the replaced hand-written production code and report lines removed and added.
- Do not edit anything under `.github/`, the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not touch `cpp/gateway/fuzz/ci.py`, `cpp/gateway/tools/ci_sanitize.py` or `docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`.
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables.
- You can be cut off without warning. Commit after every meaningful step (the tree must build at each commit), write your report file EARLY and keep it current. Leave no build directories, binaries or downloads other than the vendored library in the checkout.

REPORT: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what was replaced and what was kept as a shim (with reasons), exact commands, real pass/fail counts, the before/after measurement table, lines of production code deleted and added, anything unfinished, and defects you found outside your owned paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- exactly the files and regions each COMPONENT BRIEF below lists as owned, each brief's new harness and test files, `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` (append sections only), your report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-std-small-helpers-20261117.md`, one entry per new harness in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/targets.json`, and `tests/LINKS.txt` lines for tests you add.

TASK
POLICY: see RULES; standard library behaviour is the reference, less first-party code is the goal. This job bundles FIVE small independent components (date, console formatting, filesystem and path helpers, environment and dotenv, Headers). The maintainers' planner wrote one brief per component, included verbatim below; where a brief mentions "the supervisor", "snapshot" hashes, host tools such as `tools/run-tests.sh` or paths under `/tmp/claude-1002`, read that as: you work on this branch as cloned, you build and run the named tests yourself with your own driver on the runner, and evidence goes in your report. Where a brief asks for exact Bun parity, the RULES above win. Do the components ONE AT A TIME in this order: date, headers, environment, filesystem, console. For each: implement, build with the port flags, run its tests and the tests whose link lists include its files (plain and with ASan+UBSan), record lines removed/added, and COMMIT before starting the next, so that a cut-off loses at most one component. No third-party download is expected: use the C++20 standard library (`<chrono>`, `<filesystem>`, `<format>`, `<charconv>`) and libraries already in the build (Boost 1.92, ICU).

# Date parsing and calendar primitives

Contract v1, inventory 35. Candidate against the supervisor snapshot `55afcc8b13b2ddd10747355745da19e5264f7b76` or its exact assigned descendant after equivalent preimages are confirmed. The supervisor assigns the isolated ARM64 branch and is the only merge and registry writer. Goal is 355–425 net production lines removed from the 497-line Bun grammar and its entry point, after the new adapter.

Own paths relative to `cpp/gateway`: `src/rt/date.cpp` includes and date parser region 120–615, plus `Date::parse` at 620–626; `tests/rt/date_test.cpp` parser cases; new `fuzz/date_parse.cpp`. Header and application callers are verification surfaces. Preserve the existing time representation, UTC outputs, and wide-year arithmetic used by persisted dates.

Use C++20 locale-fixed `std::get_time` for calendar field extraction of the supported standardized forms, `std::from_chars` for bounded numeric fields and `std::chrono` calendar/duration operations within their supported range. These headers are supplied by GCC 16.1.1/libstdc++ and Apple Clang 21/libc++. Avoid depending on incomplete chrono stream parsing or narrowing wider persisted years to `std::chrono::year`. Keep only the small adapter for whole-input consumption, ISO 8601/RFC 3339 offsets and fractions, IMF-fixdate/GMT, clips and error mapping. Source supported variants from the application fixtures. Remove the Bun legacy tokenizer and date grammar. Reject malformed, ambiguous or out-of-range inputs without broadening any auth or validation decision. Use UTC and a fixed locale, with no global locale mutation.

Run from `cpp/gateway`: `tools/run-tests.sh date_test passport_sessions_test native_codex_429_differential_test codex_auth_parse_differential_test claude_code_usage_test kv_conversion_profile_json_differential_test`. Check the affected provider and storage fixtures for numeric offsets, fractional seconds, retry deadlines, existing ISO bytes and invalid timestamps. Submit a bounded date-parse harness to A for `fuzz/targets.json` registration. Keep valid date fixtures; amend only recorded generic expectations under v37. Report actual net deletion or the precise compatibility or portability gap.
